dossier.purpose: Cua Driver (`cua-driver`, v0.32.0 per libs/cua-driver/rust/VERSION:1) is a Rust cross-platform (macOS, Windows, Linux) 'background computer-use' driver in libs/cua-driver of the trycua/cua monorepo. It reads native window accessibility trees and screenshots, sends clicks/keys/scroll to apps without raising the window or moving the real pointer where the OS allows, and drives Chromium-family/Electron pages over loopback CDP via typed get_browser_state and browser_* tools. Surfaces: stdio MCP server (`cua-driver mcp`), shell CLI (`cua-driver call <tool> '<json>'` against a local `serve` daemon), in-process Python/TypeScript SDKs. For the stated web-research needs: the tool inventory (.github/scripts/cua-driver-mcp-compat/expected-tools.json:8-78; 58 base tools, +4 Linux-only, +1 Windows-only) has no tool that fetches a URL itself, extracts article/main text or metadata beyond page url and title, creates/closes/selects tabs, or exports PDF. Web path: browser_navigate (http/https/about only; libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/tools.rs:837-870) on an already-bound tab of a visible Chromium-family browser; get_browser_state (url+title, ranked outline capped at 300 nodes and 1,000 chars per node, optional viewport PNG; libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/tools.rs:307-311,454-458 and libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/semantic.rs:26-28); browser_click/type/pointer/dialog/set_input_files/download; and a legacy read-only `page` tool with get_text/query_dom (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/page.rs:253-288,461-464).

claims.claim: Gives agents 'tools to inspect and operate native desktop apps and browsers on macOS, Windows, and Linux', via 'the CLI, MCP, or typed SDKs'.
Background delivery works 'without moving your pointer or taking focus when the app and platform support it'; boundaries are deferred to the platform-support page.
Background computer-use driver for any agents; speaks MCP over stdio; drives native macOS apps without stealing focus.
MCP agents connect to `cua-driver mcp`; shell agents and automation can use `cua-driver call`; no generated Cua language client is needed.

Python (`cua_driver`) and TypeScript (`@trycua/cua-driver`) packages call the same in-process native runtime (UniFFI over a versioned C ABI), need no daemon, are for client apps rather than agents, and have no MCP facade.
`standard` is the promptless default; `bounded` admits only a reviewed manifest; `unrestricted` requires `--dangerously-bypass-approvals`; the mode is fixed at launch.

Attaching to an existing logged-in Chromium profile stays explicit (`cua-driver mcp --grant existing-profile`, host authorization, or a bounded manifest entry); Cua Driver renders no authorization modal.

The MIT Driver works without model artifacts; the optional, explicitly installed `cua-perception` extension is not MIT (AGPL-3.0-only OmniParser detector; redistribution or network hosting can trigger AGPL source obligations).
Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport stdio cua-driver -- cua-driver mcp`; a compat mode `--claude-code-computer-use-compat` 'changes only `screenshot`, which requires `pid` and `window_id`'.
macOS grants attach to the responsible app identity: install CuaDriver.app and start `open -n -g -a CuaDriver --args serve`; raw `cua-driver serve` outside the app is unsupported.
The `cua` installer offers the cua-driver MCP and skill, runs `cua auth login`, and can add skills/MCP to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others (`--select`/`--only cua-driver`).
Driver is MIT; Cua Spaces is FSL-1.1-MIT; the cua-perception extension (AGPL-3.0-only model artifact) is separate and not MIT.
Nightly macOS builds offer an opt-in encrypted local metadata-only action history (never screenshots, typed text, clipboard, raw arguments/results, trees, paths, titles or URLs).
Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw etc. are supported; Codex and Claude Agent SDK examples connect to `cua-driver mcp` without a generated client.

install.method: Driver release installer for macOS/Linux (prebuilt GitHub Release binary; SHA256SUMS always checked, Sigstore bundle checked when cosign is present)
Unified cua installer with cua-driver selected (also installs the cua CLI and runs sign-in unless skipped; delegates to the driver installer and registers skill and MCP server for detected agents)
Pinned version with mandatory signature verification (documented env overrides plus the one-liner; needs cosign on PATH)
Python SDK wheel with bundled cua-driver executable (PyPI)
TypeScript/Node SDK (npm; one native package per OS/CPU; does not bundle the executable)
Build from source (Rust 1.97.1 pinned) or install the checkout as the separate cua-driver-local product
install.command: cd libs/cua-driver/rust && cargo build -p cua-driver --release   # or: bash libs/cua-driver/scripts/install-local.sh --release --autostart

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes - release binary x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu built in a debian:11 container, glibc 2.31 floor (.github/workflows/cd-rust-cua-driver.yml:193-222,283-285); installer maps Linux-x86_64 (libs/cua-driver/scripts/_install-rust.sh:596); docs prerequisite 'x86_64 Linux desktop (X11 or XWayland, with AT-SPI 2)' (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/quickstart.mdx:13); X11 supported with toolkit limits, Wayland with compositor limits, KDE and Hyprland experimental (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/concepts/platform-support.mdx:25-26,35-42). Needs a live graphical session with session D-Bus and AT-SPI bus; headless only via a virtual X display such as Xvfb (libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver/LINUX.md:186-218; libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/lib.rs:202-217). Minimal images: `sudo apt install libxi6 at-spi2-core` (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/quickstart.mdx:57). Linux CI/E2E run on ubuntu-latest only (.github/workflows/ci-rust-linux.yml:64,119).
platforms.wsl2: unknown - neither README nor docs states WSL support. Code only detects WSL and appends a WSLg/X-server hint to 'no usable display' errors (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/lib.rs:167-218); the installer header says 'Windows via WSL or git-bash' (libs/cua-driver/scripts/_install-rust.sh:12-14) yet its error text sends Windows users to install.ps1 (libs/cua-driver/scripts/_install-rust.sh:601); no workflow in .github/workflows mentions WSL.
platforms.macos_arm64: yes - universal (arm64 + x86_64) binary, Developer-ID signed, notarized and stapled, MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET 13.0 (.github/workflows/cd-rust-cua-driver.yml:716-749,854-936); installer maps Darwin-arm64 and installs /Applications/CuaDriver.app (libs/cua-driver/scripts/_install-rust.sh:594,1242-1259); docs: 'macOS 14+, Apple Silicon or Intel; Accessibility and Screen Recording' (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/index.mdx:38); hosted CI on macos-26 (.github/workflows/e2e-rust-macos.yml:62,132). See claim_checks for the 13 vs 14 floor mismatch.
platforms.gpu: no - the driver neither requires nor uses a GPU; the optional perception extension ships a CPU ONNX Runtime ('parsing needs no GPU and no network access', docs/content/docs/cua-driver/concepts/perception-extension.mdx:63). A real or virtual display session is required instead (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/lib.rs:202-217).

integrations.cli: yes - `cua-driver call <tool> '<json-args>'` (JSON positional or stdin; `--screenshot-out-file` writes the first image block), plus list-tools, describe, mcp, mcp-config --client, serve/stop/status, doctor, skills, extension, update, telemetry (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/reference/cli/index.mdx:19-154; docs/content/docs/cua-driver/reference/cli/mcp.mdx:114-145; libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/main.rs:544-550; libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs:2322-2505). `call` requires a running `serve` daemon (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/reference/cli/mcp.mdx:118); exit codes 0/1/2/64 (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/reference/cli/index.mdx:160-167).
integrations.mcp: yes - `cua-driver mcp` stdio server speaking MCP 2026-07-28 and legacy 2025-06-18, with the skill pack served as MCP resources (libs/cua-driver/docs/mcp-protocol-and-skills.md:3-5,55-90). On Linux/Windows bare `mcp` owns its runtime and exits on stdin EOF; on macOS it proxies to CuaDriver.app (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/reference/cli/mcp.mdx:29). Optional loopback HTTP MCP (legacy protocol only): off unless CUA_DRIVER_RS_MCP_HTTP_PORT is set, binds 127.0.0.1, bearer token required (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/mcp_http.rs:32-61; libs/cua-driver/docs/mcp-protocol-and-skills.md:113-119).
integrations.sdk_or_api: yes - Python package `cua-driver` (`from cua_driver import CuaDriver`) and TypeScript `@trycua/cua-driver`, in-process via UniFFI over a versioned C ABI (libs/cua-driver/README.md:47-56,143-156; libs/cua-driver/python/README.md:8-36; libs/cua-driver/typescript/README.md:7-30; libs/cua-driver/rust/include/cua_driver_abi.h). Daemon wire protocol is line-delimited JSON over a Unix socket or named pipe (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/serve.rs:1-22). No other HTTP API found.
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: yes - Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport stdio cua-driver -- cua-driver mcp` (libs/cua-driver/README.md:200-204); `cua-driver mcp-config --client claude` prints `claude mcp add-json --scope user cua-computer-use ...` (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs:2106-2153); `cua-driver skills install` links the skill into ~/.claude/skills (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/skills.rs:43,211). Codex: `mcp-config --client codex` prints `codex mcp add cua-driver -- <path> mcp` (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs:2155-2157); skill linked into ~/.agents/skills (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/skills.rs:44,216). Claude Agent SDK and Codex SDK examples (libs/cua-driver/examples/agent-sdks/README.md:3-12,47-92). Project reports Codex 0.154.0 and Claude Code 2.1.268 interop on a clean macOS VM (libs/cua-driver/docs/mcp-protocol-and-skills.md:94-106). The cua installer can register skill and MCP server for detected agents (scripts/install/README.md:23).

readme.telemetry_and_network: Telemetry is ON by default and is not mentioned in README.md, libs/cua-driver/README.md or libs/cua-driver/rust/README.md (grep found none); it is disclosed in docs/content/docs/cua-driver/guides/operate.mdx:295-319, libs/cua-driver/scripts/README.md:74-79 and installer output (libs/cua-driver/scripts/_install-rust.sh:1522-1530). Code: fixed-name events (install, release installed, CLI completed, MCP session/tool completed, agent session, permissions gate, update checked/applied) with bounded properties (version, OS family/major, arch, transport, built-in tool names else 'other', bucketed durations) are POSTed to PostHog EU https://eu.i.posthog.com/capture/ with an embedded project key, a persistent pseudonymous installation ID as distinct_id, $geoip_disable=true, $process_person_profile=false, no $ip, 3 s timeout (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/telemetry.rs:25-29,71-87,2108-2148,2220-2237). Opt-out precedence: DO_NOT_TRACK, CUA_DRIVER_RS_TELEMETRY_ENABLED, CUA_TELEMETRY_ENABLED, CUA_TELEMETRY, ~/.cua/config.toml telemetry off, persisted `cua-driver telemetry disable` (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/telemetry.rs:216-242); the project's own release workflow sets CUA_TELEMETRY=0 and DO_NOT_TRACK=1 (.github/workflows/cd-rust-cua-driver.yml:87-90). Separate update check: GitHub Releases API on `mcp`, `serve`, `doctor`, at most about once per 20 h, opt-out CUA_DRIVER_RS_UPDATE_CHECK=false or update_check_enabled=false (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/version_check.rs:1-26,50-70). Explicit-only downloads: `skills install` from a GitHub release asset (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/skills.rs:680-712), `extension install` for the optional perception extension with signed catalog (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/concepts/perception-extension.mdx:72-94), `update --apply` re-runs https://cua.ai/driver/install.sh (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/updater.rs:91-93); `install_ffmpeg` runs an OS package manager when confirm=true (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/ffmpeg_install.rs:49-85). The driver has no HTTP client for fetching pages: the only HTTP crate is `ureq` in the binary crate (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/Cargo.toml:33) and every raw socket in core/platform crates targets 127.0.0.1 CDP ports; the CDP client accepts only loopback ws:// (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/cdp_ws.rs:12-13,87-102), so page loading happens inside the browser. No account or API key is needed for the direct driver installer or runtime, and the driver 'never calls a model API' (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/guides/connect-your-agent.mdx:11-12); the unified `cua` installer path additionally runs `cua auth login` unless `--no-onboarding` (README.md:111; scripts/install/README.md:45). Installers fetch from GitHub Releases and cua.ai (libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.sh:42,121-125; libs/cua-driver/scripts/_install-rust.sh:891,1581).

entry_points.what: `cua-driver` binary (default-run): dispatches mcp (stdio MCP), serve (daemon), call, mcp-config, skills, extension, update, telemetry (main.rs:1-42,544-552)
CLI command definitions, per-client mcp-config snippets, run_call with --screenshot-out-file (cli.rs:2106-2157,2322-2505)
daemon: line-delimited JSON over Unix socket/named pipe serving call/list/describe/shutdown (serve.rs:1-22)
stdio MCP adapter that owns the SDK runtime directly or forwards to a daemon (proxy.rs:1-17)
optional loopback-only HTTP MCP listener (off unless CUA_DRIVER_RS_MCP_HTTP_PORT is set)
cdylib/rlib libcua_driver_sdk (UniFFI + C ABI header rust/include/cua_driver_abi.h) consumed by the Python and Node SDKs
console script `cua-driver = cua_driver.__main__:main`; wheel bundles the executable and native library (pyproject.toml:49-63)

code.architecture: Cargo workspace libs/cua-driver/rust (15 crates; libs/cua-driver/rust/Cargo.toml:2-19). cua-driver-core is the platform-independent core: MCP/JSON-RPC dispatch (src/server.rs, mcp_wire.rs, protocol.rs), tool model/registry (tool.rs), authorization, permission modes, capability manifests and Rego/YAML policy (authorization.rs, session_manifest.rs, policy.rs), sessions (session.rs; 5-minute default idle TTL at :30), daemon wire protocol (daemon.rs), recording, legacy `page` tool (page.rs), and the typed browser engine in src/browser/ (engine.rs, tools.rs, semantic.rs, cdp_ws.rs with 20 s call / 10 s connect timeouts and an allow-list for existing-profile sockets, prepare.rs, store.rs, download.rs, pointer.rs). cua-driver-contract holds typed inputs/outputs and schemas. platform-macos (AX, ScreenCaptureKit, CGEvent/SkyLight), platform-windows (UIA, Win32, Graphics Capture) and platform-linux (AT-SPI over D-Bus, X11/XTest, Wayland protocols, portals/libei) are selected by cfg(target_os). The cua-driver binary crate adds CLI, daemon, stdio proxy, optional HTTP, telemetry, updater, skills and extension manager. cua-driver-sdk is the in-process SDK/C ABI; cursor-overlay/cursor-theme-cli draw the agent cursor; cua-perception is the optional ONNX worker (AGPL models, installed separately); cua-driver-uia is a Windows UIAccess worker; testkit/e2e are never shipped. Python and TypeScript packages wrap the SDK; the skill pack in libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver is embedded and served as MCP resources. Web interaction: bind a native browser window with get_browser_state(pid, window_id), which mints session-scoped target/tab/ref capabilities (explicit non-default session label required, libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/tools.rs:53-62), then browser_* actions over CDP. The browser is either a headed isolated-profile Chromium launched by browser_prepare (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/prepare.rs:393-408) or an existing profile attached under an explicit grant. Bounded mode can restrict browser work to listed origins (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/guides/permissions.mdx:125-163).
code.packaging_and_release: Release Please creates the cua-driver-rs-v* tag and draft; the tag push runs .github/workflows/cd-rust-cua-driver.yml:3-20,62-65, which builds Linux x86_64 and arm64 (native runners inside debian:11, glibc 2.31 floor, cargo build --locked --release; :193-222,283-285), Windows x86_64/arm64 (Authenticode-signed, signer verified; :326-338,449-470) and a macOS universal binary plus notarized CuaDriver.app (:716-749,854-936), then runs E2E gates and signature verification before the release job can publish (:1195-1255). Assets: cua-driver-rs-v<ver>-linux-{x86_64,arm64}-binary.tar.gz (+ full tarball with LICENSE/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES), macOS universal tarballs, Windows zips, skills tarball, installer scripts, Hyprland plugin source tarballs (:293-314,1327-1387). Integrity: SHA256SUMS plus a keyless Sigstore cosign bundle (<asset>.sigstore.json) for every asset and for SHA256SUMS, issued to the workflow at the tag (:1419-1452). Installers always verify SHA256SUMS (required from 0.31.0) and refuse a release lacking the Sigstore bundle from 0.32.0, verifying it only if cosign is installed unless --require-signature (libs/cua-driver/scripts/_install-rust.sh:940-1049). No SBOM or SLSA/build-provenance attestation found for driver assets (contrast the perception extension, docs/content/docs/cua-driver/concepts/perception-extension.mdx:72-76). Python wheels (macOS, Linux x86_64/arm64, Windows x86_64/arm64; hatchling) are uploaded to PyPI via twine token with no attestation; npm packages use `npm publish --provenance` (.github/workflows/cd-py-cua-driver.yml:127-150,225-235,364-378). Nightly workflow (cron 17 4 * * *) publishes immutable nightlies with checksums.txt (.github/workflows/nightly-cua-driver.yml:3-6,94-97). Withdrawn versions list blocks 0.28.3, which shipped an unsigned macOS app (.github/release-state/cua-driver-rs-withdrawn-versions:3).
code.tests_and_ci: Rust built-in harness via cargo test: about 85 files under libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/*/tests (34 desktop E2E in cua-driver-e2e, 27 hermetic protocol/CLI tests in cua-driver, 13 in cua-driver-core) plus #[test]/#[tokio::test] modules in 327 src files; cargo-fuzz with 4 targets (libs/cua-driver/rust/fuzz/fuzz_targets: mcp_request, registry_invoke, tool_arguments, typed_input_json); GUI fixture apps (AppKit, SwiftUI, GTK, WPF, WinUI3, Electron, Tauri, web) in libs/cua-driver/tests/fixtures. About 50 non-Rust test files: python/tests (6), typescript/test (5, node --test), scripts/tests (17 installer py/sh/ps1), examples/jev-use/python/tests (23). About 30 driver-related workflows in .github/workflows: ci-rust-linux/macos/windows.yml (unit + Xvfb X11 input/capture), ci-rust-format.yml (cargo fmt on 3 OSes), ci-cua-driver-quick.yml, ci-driver-mcp-candidate.yml (modern MCP client probe on Linux/macOS/Windows), ci-cua-driver-valgrind.yml, fuzz-cua-driver.yml (PR + nightly cron), ci-distro-compat-cua-driver.yml (released binary on debian:12, ubuntu 22.04/24.04, rocky 9, fedora 41), ci-installers.yml, monitor-branded-installers.yml (6-hourly canary of cua.ai installers), license-check.yml, ci-lockfiles.yml; E2E: e2e-rust-linux.yml (X11/Openbox), e2e-rust-linux-wayland.yml (Sway, Sway+XWayland, nested), e2e-rust-macos.yml (hosted macos-26 / Lume VM), e2e-rust-windows.yml, e2e-rust-standalone-browsers.yml (Chrome on Ubuntu; Chrome+Edge on Windows). The standalone-browser E2E drives browser tools through the MCP transport, not CLI call (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-e2e/tests/standalone_browser_behavior_test.rs:27,758-800). Linux CI runs on ubuntu-latest only.
code.dependencies: Rust workspace manifest libs/cua-driver/rust/Cargo.toml (27 workspace dependencies); libs/cua-driver/rust/Cargo.lock pins 637 packages; builds use --locked; toolchain pinned to 1.97.1 (libs/cua-driver/rust/rust-toolchain.toml:2). Direct normal-dependency counts per crate manifest under libs/cua-driver/rust/crates: cua-driver 28 (+1-3 per-OS), cua-driver-core 30 (2 optional: regex, regorus), cua-driver-contract 4, cua-driver-sdk 11 (+1-2 per-OS), cursor-overlay 13, cursor-theme-cli 8, cua-perception 9 (incl. ort 2.0.0-rc.10, libloading), pip-preview 1, cua-driver-bindgen 2, cua-driver-uia 8 (Windows only), platform-linux 16 + 29 Linux-only (6 optional), platform-macos 15 + 17 macOS-only, platform-windows 14 + 5 Windows-only; testkit (10) and e2e (17 dev-deps) are never shipped. Notable: tokio, serde, ureq 3 (telemetry/update/skills HTTP), ring, cap-std, tokio-tungstenite (loopback CDP), regorus, uniffi 0.31.0, atspi/zbus/x11rb/wayland-client/ashpd (Linux), objc2/core-graphics/screencapturekit (macOS), windows 0.58/0.61. Path dependency outside the driver tree: libs/cua/crates/cua-telemetry (config reader only; 7 deps). Python libs/cua-driver/python/pyproject.toml: 0 runtime deps (hatchling build; optional pytest). TypeScript libs/cua-driver/typescript/package.json: 2 runtime deps (@ubjs/core, @ubjs/node 0.31.0-3) and 5 dev deps. No cargo-audit/cargo-deny/Dependabot/Renovate/CodeQL/OSV configuration found under .github.
code.security_policy: SECURITY.md at the repo root (covers all components including Cua Driver): private reporting through GitHub private vulnerability reporting (no dedicated mailbox or security.txt yet); targets: acknowledgment in 2 business days, initial assessment in 5, remediation timeline in 10; only the current released version of each component is supported; includes a good-faith safe-harbor section (SECURITY.md:3-38,40-90).

claim_checks.claim: Shell-oriented agents and automation can use `cua-driver call` (libs/cua-driver/README.md:44-47); docs add that every tool also runs from the shell with the same code path (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/reference/mcp-tools/index.mdx:13).
claim_checks.evidence: `call` is wired to cli::run_call (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/main.rs:544-550) with --screenshot-out-file (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs:2322-2505). But it needs a running serve daemon (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/reference/cli/mcp.mdx:118); typed browser tools refuse any call without an explicit non-default session label, so every shell step must repeat it (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/tools.rs:53-62; libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver/RUNTIME.md:20-24); sessions idle-expire after 5 minutes (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/session.rs:30); browser_download is refused on a plain CLI call because its MCP-host approval flag is injected only for live MCP proxy sessions (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/serve.rs:155-164; libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/download.rs:81-87,296-302); BROWSER.md says its examples are not separate shell commands and recommends one persistent MCP connection (libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver/BROWSER.md:38-40,82-84); the browser E2E suite uses the MCP transport only (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-e2e/tests/standalone_browser_behavior_test.rs:27,758-800).

claim_checks.claim: Background delivery lets agents work without moving your pointer or taking focus when the app and platform support it (README.md:132).
claim_checks.evidence: Qualified by the README itself. For browsers, trusted CDP clicks default to background posture and are refused with browser_input_trust_unavailable on standalone Chromium on macOS and Linux (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/tools.rs:1033-1055; libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver/BROWSER.md:351-356,479-483); the dom_event alternative stays in the background but returns an unverifiable effect (libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver/BROWSER.md:357-372); delivery_mode foreground accepts window activation. Only Windows Chrome/Edge have validated trusted background delivery (libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver/BROWSER.md:353-356).

claim_checks.claim: Tools to inspect and operate native desktop apps and browsers on macOS, Windows, and Linux (README.md:132).
claim_checks.evidence: Typed browser tools cover Chromium-family browsers and single-page Electron; Safari, Firefox, Tauri, WKWebView, WebKitGTK and split-process WebView2 get native-only state or browser_route_unavailable (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/guides/browsers.mdx:8-14; libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver/BROWSER.md:459-462,477-487). The tool inventory has no URL-fetch, article-text, tab create/close/select, select-option or PDF tool (.github/scripts/cua-driver-mcp-compat/expected-tools.json:8-78; libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/store.rs:34-39); screenshots are viewport PNG only (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/tools.rs:307-311); a grep of libs/cua-driver for printToPDF/pdf found only fixtures and a redaction test string (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/tool.rs:5806,5818).

claim_checks.claim: Attaching to an existing logged-in Chromium profile remains explicit: `cua-driver mcp --grant existing-profile`; no Cua modal (libs/cua-driver/README.md:86-97).
claim_checks.evidence: The grant is normalised into an immutable launcher grant, never read from env or tool arguments (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/authorization.rs:21-39); flag documented in CLI help (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs:4076); existing-profile sockets are limited to a fixed CDP method allow-list (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/cdp_ws.rs:33-81); standard mode otherwise denies the operation (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/guides/permissions.mdx:55).

claim_checks.claim: `standard` is the promptless default; `bounded` admits only a reviewed manifest; `unrestricted` requires `--dangerously-bypass-approvals` (libs/cua-driver/README.md:75-77).
claim_checks.evidence: An unset mode resolves to standard (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/authorization.rs:1286-1291); unrestricted is selected only with the bypass flag and prints a DANGER banner (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/main.rs:55-106); docs: unrestricted alone fails closed and bounded needs a manifest (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/guides/permissions.mdx:28-29,42,70-72). Caveat: standard allows input to every app without prompts (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/guides/connect-your-agent.mdx:63-69).

README is stale; code wins. The screenshot tool and its compat variant were removed in PR #1692 (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/tools/impl_.rs:9742-9746; libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs:10132-10149); the flag is a documented no-op ('there is no standalone screenshot tool', libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs:4080); `mcp-config --client claude` no longer emits it and registers `cua-computer-use` via claude mcp add-json (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs:2106-2153); expected-tools.json has no screenshot tool (.github/scripts/cua-driver-mcp-compat/expected-tools.json:8-78). Window screenshots come from get_window_state or get_browser_state include_screenshot.

claim_checks.claim: The default MIT Driver works without model artifacts; the optional cua-perception extension is explicit-install and AGPL-3.0-only (libs/cua-driver/README.md:8-26).
claim_checks.evidence: parse_visual_regions returns a stable not_installed error when the extension is absent (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/perception_tools.rs:649-659); installation is only via install_extension / `cua-driver extension install` (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/concepts/perception-extension.mdx:42-44,89-94); the extension crate is versioned separately (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-perception/Cargo.toml:3); AGPL text ships with the models (LICENSING.md:65-66).

claim_checks.claim: Linux scope: docs require an 'x86_64 Linux desktop' (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/quickstart.mdx:13) and the Python README lists Linux x86_64 only (libs/cua-driver/python/README.md:194-199).
claim_checks.evidence: The release workflow also builds linux-arm64 (.github/workflows/cd-rust-cua-driver.yml:204-206), the installer maps Linux-aarch64 (libs/cua-driver/scripts/_install-rust.sh:597,600) and wheels/npm include Linux arm64 (.github/workflows/cd-py-cua-driver.yml:143-144,277,298), but Linux CI and E2E run only on ubuntu-latest (.github/workflows/ci-rust-linux.yml:64,119), so arm64 behavior has no CI evidence.

claim_checks.claim: macOS minimum is 14+ in prose docs (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/quickstart.mdx:13; docs/content/docs/cua-driver/index.mdx:38) but 13+ in the Python README (libs/cua-driver/python/README.md:196).
claim_checks.evidence: Code floor is 13.0: LSMinimumSystemVersion 13.0 (libs/cua-driver/rust/scripts/CuaDriverBundle/Contents/Info.plist:68-69) and MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET 13.0 (libs/cua-driver/rust/.cargo/config.toml:2; .github/workflows/cd-rust-cua-driver.yml:719,724). Some features need newer macOS: window capture filter info 14+ (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/capture.rs:495) and video recording 15+ (libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver/RECORDING.md:51). Docs disagree with each other; the code floor is 13.0.

claim_checks.claim: Docs: Cua Driver sends content-free, pseudonymous usage events to PostHog's EU endpoint, on by default (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/guides/operate.mdx:297-298); neither README mentions telemetry.
claim_checks.evidence: Default-on with env/config opt-outs (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/telemetry.rs:216-242); payload builder uses fixed event names and bounded properties, GeoIP disabled, no $ip (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/telemetry.rs:9-12,2108-2148); PostHog EU URL and embedded key (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/telemetry.rs:25-26).

risks: Scope: no URL-fetch, main-text-with-metadata, PDF or tab-management tool exists (.github/scripts/cua-driver-mcp-compat/expected-tools.json:8-78). browser_navigate only drives a tab of an already-bound browser (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/tools.rs:837-870); snapshots return page url+title and a ranked outline, not author/date/canonical metadata or response status/headers (same file:454-458); browser_download deliberately returns no source URL or filename (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/download.rs:5,46); screenshots are viewport-only PNG (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/tools.rs:307-311); typed routes cover Chromium-family only (libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver/BROWSER.md:459-462).

Shell path is daemon-backed and stateful: `cua-driver call` needs a standing `serve` daemon (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/reference/cli/mcp.mdx:118), browser capabilities need a repeated explicit session label and expire after 5 idle minutes (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/tools.rs:53-62; libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/session.rs:30), browser_download is refused from plain CLI calls (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/serve.rs:155-164), BROWSER.md recommends one persistent MCP connection (libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver/BROWSER.md:38-40,82-84), and CI drives the browser tools over MCP, not CLI (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-e2e/tests/standalone_browser_behavior_test.rs:27,758-800).

Platform prerequisites: needs a live graphical session and an installed Chrome/Chromium/Edge; browser_prepare launches a headed isolated-profile browser with no --headless flag (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/prepare.rs:393-408) from platform-attested system installs only (libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver/BROWSER.md:132-147). Linux needs AT-SPI plus session D-Bus (libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver/LINUX.md:186-218) and --force-renderer-accessibility for existing-profile setup, which recognises English UI labels only (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/guides/browsers.mdx:174-176); macOS needs Accessibility and Screen Recording grants on CuaDriver.app (libs/cua-driver/README.md:216-227); GNOME needs a Shell helper and re-login (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/quickstart.mdx:59-65); Linux arm64 is built but not CI-tested; WSL2 is undocumented; trusted browser clicks refuse background delivery on macOS/Linux (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/tools.rs:1033-1055).

Fast-moving beta: releases 0.30.4 (2026-09-28), 0.31.0 (2026-09-29, a listed BREAKING CHANGE to element-token resolution) and 0.32.0 (2026-10-01) (libs/cua-driver/rust/CHANGELOG.md:9-46); 0.28.3 was withdrawn after shipping an unsigned macOS app (.github/release-state/cua-driver-rs-withdrawn-versions:3); PyPI classifier is Beta (libs/cua-driver/python/pyproject.toml:23) and the installer calls the Rust driver 'BETA-stage' (libs/cua-driver/scripts/_install-rust.sh:834); the SDK READMEs announce a next breaking typed-window release (libs/cua-driver/python/README.md:95-100). The pinned tag cua-spaces-v0.2.0 is a Cua Spaces release, not a driver release: this tree is driver 0.32.0 plus an Unreleased fix (libs/cua-driver/rust/CHANGELOG.md:3-7), so a build from this commit is not identical to published cua-driver-rs-v0.32.0 assets.

Telemetry is default-on (PostHog EU, persistent pseudonymous ID), absent from the READMEs, plus a separate default-on GitHub update check; opting out needs env/config (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/telemetry.rs:25-26,216-242; libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/version_check.rs:50-70); the installer starts a background install event after a notice (libs/cua-driver/scripts/_install-rust.sh:1522-1530).

Installer trust chain: README install is curl-to-bash from cua.ai; install.sh then downloads _install-rust.sh from cua.ai at run time and executes it (libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.sh:42,121-125), outside SHA256SUMS/Sigstore coverage; the binary checksum comes from the same GitHub release as the tarball, and Sigstore verification runs only when cosign is installed unless --require-signature is set (libs/cua-driver/scripts/_install-rust.sh:1022-1036); the endpoint monitor only greps for a marker string (.github/workflows/monitor-branded-installers.yml:106-116), so equality of cua.ai content with repository files could not be verified.

Security posture: default standard mode allows observation and input to every app without prompts (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/guides/permissions.mdx:25-29,47-56); existing-profile CDP attach exposes cookies/storage to same-user processes (libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver/BROWSER.md:159-166); page text is untrusted prompt-injection surface (libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver/BROWSER.md:322-324); opt-in trajectory recordings keep tool arguments, including browser_type/type_text text, redacting only a few fields (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/tool.rs:5629-5674; libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/recording.rs:916-921); install_ffmpeg can run `sudo -n` plus a package manager when confirm=true (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/ffmpeg_install.rs:56-85); a bounded origin list cannot stop a page redirecting after a click (docs/content/docs/cua-driver/guides/permissions.mdx:268-270).

Licensing and supply chain: driver is MIT (LICENSE.md) but the repo mixes licenses: the optional perception extension is AGPL-3.0-only with network-use source obligations (libs/cua-driver/README.md:19-26), Cua Spaces is FSL-1.1-MIT (LICENSING.md:12-16,72-96), cua-som is AGPL-3.0-or-later (README.md:256-258). Cargo.lock pins 637 packages including pre-release ort 2.0.0-rc.10 (libs/cua-driver/rust/Cargo.toml:46); no dependency-audit tooling (cargo-audit, cargo-deny, Dependabot, Renovate, CodeQL, OSV) found in .github; PyPI wheels are uploaded with a token and no attestation (.github/workflows/cd-py-cua-driver.yml:225-235); no SBOM/provenance for driver binaries.

checks.statement: Driver release installer for macOS/Linux (prebuilt GitHub Release binary; SHA256SUMS always checked, Sigstore bundle checked when cosign is present): /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/driver/install.sh)"
checks.note: The exact command is at README.md:137 and quickstart.mdx:25 (macOS) and :52 (Linux). install.sh downloads the GitHub release (header at lines 2-3). verify_release_tarball always checks SHA256SUMS: it is required from 0.31.0, and older releases without it install with a warning. It requires a Sigstore bundle from 0.32.0 but runs cosign verify-blob only when cosign is on PATH, unless --require-signature is set (_install-rust.sh:1021-1036). So the parenthetical holds for the current 0.32.0 release.

LICENSE.md is the standard MIT text (Copyright 2025 Cua AI, Inc.). README.md:248 and LICENSING.md:13,134 name Cua Driver as MIT. The driver's Rust workspace (all crates use license.workspace), the PyPI package and the npm package all declare MIT. The repo is mixed-license: Spaces is FSL-1.1-MIT and the optional cua-perception models are AGPL-3.0-only. The dossier's risks section already discloses this.

checks.statement: yes - release binary x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu built in a debian:11 container with a glibc 2.31 floor; installer maps Linux-x86_64; docs require an x86_64 Linux desktop (X11 or XWayland, AT-SPI 2); X11/Wayland supported with limits, KDE and Hyprland experimental; needs a live graphical session with session D-Bus and AT-SPI, headless only via Xvfb; minimal images need libxi6 at-spi2-core; Linux CI/E2E on ubuntu-latest only
checks.note: Every sub-claim matches. The build matrix pairs x86_64 with x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu inside image debian:11, with the glibc 2.31 floor explained at lines 214-215, and builds with cargo build --locked --release (:285). The installer maps Linux-x86_64 to linux-x86_64 (:596). KDE/KWin (:40) and Hyprland (:41) are marked Experimental. lib.rs:212-213 says 'Xvfb for headless'. One small imprecision: the ci-rust-linux.yml:64 job runs an archlinux container on ubuntu-latest, and ci-driver-mcp-candidate.yml:31 pins ubuntu-24.04, which is the same hosted x86_64 image. The point that no arm64 or other runner tests Linux still stands.

checks.statement: yes - `cua-driver mcp` stdio server speaking MCP 2026-07-28 and legacy 2025-06-18 with the skill pack served as MCP resources; Linux/Windows bare mcp owns its runtime and exits on stdin EOF, macOS proxies to CuaDriver.app; optional loopback HTTP MCP (legacy only), off unless CUA_DRIVER_RS_MCP_HTTP_PORT is set, binds 127.0.0.1, bearer token required
checks.note: The protocol versions are at doc lines 3-4. The embedded eight-file skill pack is read via skills/list, skills/get and resources/read (55-90). mcp.mdx:29 states the Linux/Windows vs macOS runtime ownership word for word. In mcp_http.rs, the port is None unless the env var is set (34-54) and the listener binds [127,0,0,1] (60). spawn() fails closed without CUA_DRIVER_RS_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, which must be 32-4096 characters (58, 371-390), and requests are checked against a Bearer scheme (339). HTTP stays on legacy MCP (doc 115-116).

checks.statement: 'Tools to inspect and operate native desktop apps and browsers on macOS, Windows, and Linux' is verified as partial: typed browser tools cover Chromium-family and single-page Electron only; the inventory has no URL-fetch, article-text, tab create/close/select, select-option or PDF tool; screenshots are viewport PNG only; a pdf grep finds only a test string
checks.note: expected-tools.json lists 58 base tools plus 4 Linux-only and 1 Windows-only. None fetches, extracts articles, manages tabs, selects options or prints PDFs. BrowserActionKind is limited to Click/Type/Upload/Pointer/Scroll. include_screenshot captures 'the exact tab viewport as PNG'. A grep of the driver crates for pdf hits only '/private/document.pdf' at tool.rs:5806,5818. BROWSER.md:455 sends tabs to the native loop. The names browser_new_tab, browser_close_tab and browser_select_tab exist only in a cursor-animation classifier (cua-driver-contract/src/cursor.rs:232-235) and are not registered tools. The legacy page get_text returns whole-page visible text (page.rs:269), not main-article extraction, so 'no article-text tool' holds.
